Chapter 3: Asking Small Questions to Spark Change.
Let’s dive into one of the most powerful tools in the Kaizen approach—small questions. Think about those moments when you’re faced with a big challenge, or you’ve set an ambitious goal. Most of us feel a wave of anxiety, maybe even a bit of resistance. The task just seems... too much, doesn’t it? But here’s where small questions come in.
When you ask yourself gentle, focused questions, you’re not provoking fear—you’re engaging your mind’s natural curiosity and creativity. Instead of demanding instant solutions or drastic action, small questions invite you to reflect and make tiny steps forward. Over time, these little prompts can actually uncover insights and ideas you’d never expect.
For example, let’s say you’re struggling to find motivation for exercise. Rather than pushing yourself with, “I have to work out for an hour today,” you could ask, “What’s one movement I could do today that would make me feel just a little better?” It’s not about running a marathon—it’s about choosing one small, manageable action. The amazing thing? Your mind, sensing no threat, becomes more open and creative in response.
This technique isn’t just for fitness. You can use it anywhere in your life.
In relationships, you might ask, “What’s one small thing I could do to show appreciation today?” At work, “What’s one step I could take to make this project easier?” And for personal growth, “What’s one thought I could focus on to feel more positive?”
The beauty of small questions is how they gently bypass your mind’s tendency to shut down in the face of big demands. Instead, they open the door to possibility—inviting you to explore, bit by bit, and discover what’s truly possible.
So, how do you make the most of this approach? Here are a few tips:
First, keep your questions specific, and focus on actions you can actually take right now. Make it a habit to ask these questions regularly, giving your mind space and time to reflect. Be patient—sometimes, the answers come slowly, but they will come. And most importantly, use whatever answers you get as a springboard for small, consistent steps forward.
Over time, you’ll notice a shift. Instead of feeling overwhelmed by the need for big, dramatic change, you’ll start approaching challenges with curiosity and a quiet confidence. Your mind, engaged by these gentle questions, becomes your ally in the process of growth.
